observable_definition: Implemented and derivative-tested: squared excess of local point distance outside a calibrated spatial tolerance. A coordinate intervention to be tested, not a proven affinity rule.
predicted_execution_response: Measured current-program response only; no terminal-affinity gradient. Expect active_updates and nonzero_updates comparable to R11_v2 (40/40) with no atom or cumulative clipping, since dose and controller are unchanged. Expect point_rms_A and target_error_mean to fall to a nonzero plateau set by base_band_A rather than continuing toward zero, and current_gradient_rms_mean to decay faster once points enter the band. Assignment_switch_fraction should remain near zero as in R11_v2.
predicted_terminal_response: Proposed, not measured: terminal mean_all_pic50 and best_qualified_pic50 for the point_band arm relative to R11_v2 (mean_all_pic50 7.6281831463178, best_qualified_pic50 8.12820816040039, U_tau 0.0, n_qualified 24). Direction is not asserted; the discriminating quantity is whether the band-limited arm changes U_tau or the qualified count at fixed region and dose.
scientific_hypothesis: Replacing the unbounded pointwise pseudo-Huber pull with a band-limited squared-excess objective on the same NO-region support will change the local displacement distribution: matched local points will be driven to within the calibrated tolerance band rather than continuing to contract toward exact teacher coordinates. Because the band removes residual inward force once a point is inside tolerance, the retained local geometry should be less over-contracted at the terminal state, and the terminal affinity mean guard may improve relative to R11_v2 without changing the region or dose.
